walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Transmission — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Transmission brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Transmission.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: Any item, randomly.
The first one added (FIFO).
To make the function run faster.
The most recently added (top) - LIFO.

mcqs.q: Why must a recursive function have a base case?
options: Variables that change type at runtime.
Without it, the function calls itself indefinitely, causing a stack overflow.
Because the syntax requires it.
To make the function run faster.
Having multiple classes with the same name.
To make the function run faster.
Variables that change type at runtime.
The ability of different classes to respond to the same method call in their own way.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Casting”?
options: Converting a value from one data type to another, e.g., int("5") gives integer 5.
Whole number with no fractional part, positive, negative or zero (e.g., 7, -42, 0).
Single letter, digit or symbol, typically stored using ASCII or Unicode codes.
Ordered sequence of characters, used to store text such as names or sentences.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Boolean”?
options: Single letter, digit or symbol, typically stored using ASCII or Unicode codes.
Number with a fractional part stored using floating-point representation (e.g., 3.14).
Converting a value from one data type to another, e.g., int("5") gives integer 5.
Data type with only two possible values: True or False, used for logical conditions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Real / float”?

Whole number with no fractional part, positive, negative or zero (e.g., 7, -42, 0).
Number with a fractional part stored using floating-point representation (e.g., 3.14).
Single letter, digit or symbol, typically stored using ASCII or Unicode codes.
